title: Classification of Regular Polytopes in Higher Dimensions
description: Extends the Platonic solids classification to 4D and higher dimensions using the Coxeter-Schlaefli determinant. Proves there are exactly 6 regular 4-polytopes, 3 regular 5-polytopes, and verifies the high-dimensional stabilization pattern.

meta.author: Schlaefli (1852), Coxeter (1973); formalized here

mathlibDependencies.description: Computational decision procedure for finite verification
Finite set enumeration of Schlaefli symbols

originalContributions: Exact arithmetic in Z[sqrt(5)] for Schlaefli determinant computation
4D classification: exactly 6 regular polytopes via Coxeter-Schlaefli determinant
5D classification: exactly 3 regular polytopes (simplex, hypercube, cross-polytope)
Proof that {4,3,...,3,4} always gives Euclidean tiling (determinant = 0)
Combinatorial data (V,E,F,C) for all 6 regular 4-polytopes with Euler verification
Duality relationships: 5-cell and 24-cell are self-dual, 8-cell/16-cell and 120-cell/600-cell form dual pairs
meta.assumptions: The classification counts (5 Platonic solids, 6 regular 4-polytopes, 3 regular 5-polytopes) and the Schlaefli determinant sign tests are discharged by native_decide, which depends on Lean.ofReduceBool (the proof is not axiom-free). The Schlaefli determinant computation uses exact arithmetic in Z[sqrt(5)] to determine the sign of sin^2(pi/p)*sin^2(pi/r) - cos^2(pi/q) for all candidate symbols.

overview.historicalContext: Ludwig Schlaefli (1852) classified regular polytopes in all dimensions, extending Euclid's classification of the 5 Platonic solids. He discovered that dimension 4 is exceptional: it admits 6 regular polytopes, including the remarkable 24-cell which has no analog in any other dimension. For dimensions 5 and above, only three families survive: the simplex, hypercube, and cross-polytope. H.S.M. Coxeter later systematized this theory using reflection groups and Gram matrices, providing the algebraic framework used in this formalization.
overview.problemStatement:
**Classification of Regular Polytopes**:

- **Dimension 3**: 5 regular polytopes (Platonic solids)
- **Dimension 4**: 6 regular polytopes (5-cell, 8-cell, 16-cell, 24-cell, 120-cell, 600-cell)
- **Dimension n >= 5**: 3 regular polytopes (n-simplex, n-hypercube, n-cross-polytope)

The 4D case is the richest, containing three exceptional polytopes that exist in no other dimension.
overview.text: Classification of regular polytopes via the Coxeter-Schlaefli determinant, covering dimensions 3 through 6 with the high-dimensional stabilization pattern.
overview.proofStrategy:
**Proof via Coxeter-Schlaefli Determinant**:

1. A regular n-polytope with Schlaefli symbol {p1,...,pn-1} exists iff the Gram matrix determinant is positive.

2. For 4D {p,q,r}: both {p,q} and {q,r} must be Platonic solid symbols, AND the determinant Delta = sin^2(pi/p)*sin^2(pi/r) - cos^2(pi/q) > 0.

3. Exact computation in Z[sqrt(5)] determines the sign for all 11 candidates, yielding exactly 6 valid symbols.

4. For 5D: recursive determinant check eliminates all exceptional 4D polytopes.

5. For n >= 5: only {3,...,3}, {4,3,...,3}, {3,...,3,4} survive (proved by determinant recurrence).
keyInsights: The Coxeter-Schlaefli determinant sin^2(pi/p)*sin^2(pi/r) - cos^2(pi/q) reduces higher-dimensional classification to arithmetic in Z[sqrt(5)]
The 120-cell and 600-cell barely exist: their 4D determinant 14-6*sqrt(5) is positive because 196 > 180, but the 5D extension 64-32*sqrt(5) is negative because 4096 < 5120
The 24-cell {3,4,3} is self-dual and exists only in dimension 4 -- a remarkable exception
{4,3,...,3,4} always has Schlaefli determinant exactly 0 (Euclidean tiling in every dimension >= 4)
The all-3s sequence {3,...,3} has determinant (n+1)/2^n, decaying but always positive
Dimension 4 is the 'golden dimension' with 6 regular polytopes -- more than any other dimension

sections.title: Module Header and Overview
sections.summary: Module docstring extending the Platonic solids classification (Wiedijk #50) to 4D and higher: 6 regular polytopes in 4D, 3 in n >= 5. States the Schläfli-symbol / Coxeter-Schläfli determinant criterion, lists the 6 regular 4-polytopes and 3 infinite families, references, imports, and the RegularPolytopes namespace.
sections.mathContext: A regular n-polytope has a Schläfli symbol {p_1,...,p_{n-1}}; validity requires each consecutive pair to be a valid lower-dimensional symbol and the Coxeter-Schläfli determinant (angle-defect condition) to be positive.

sections.title: PART 1: Exact Arithmetic in Z[sqrt(5)]
sections.summary: The QSqrt5 structure (a + b*sqrt(5), a,b in Z) with mul, sub, scale, and isPositive for exact computation of Schläfli determinants involving the golden ratio.
sections.mathContext: The ring Z[sqrt(5)] = {a + b*sqrt(5) : a,b in Z} enables exact arithmetic with cos^2(pi/5) = (3+sqrt(5))/8. Positivity checking reduces to integer comparison: a + b*sqrt(5) > 0 iff a^2 > 5b^2 (when signs differ).

sections.title: PART 2: Trigonometric Values (Scaled by 8)
sections.summary: sinSqScaled and cosSqScaled give 8*sin^2(pi/n) and 8*cos^2(pi/n) as QSqrt5 elements for n in {3,4,5}, with trig_identity_3/4/5 confirming the stored values.
sections.mathContext: sin^2(pi/3) = 3/4, sin^2(pi/4) = 1/2, sin^2(pi/5) = (5-sqrt(5))/8. These are the only values needed since the Platonic solids have p,q in {3,4,5}.

sections.title: PART 3: The 3D Constraint (Recalled)
sections.summary: validPairs3D (the 5 Platonic pairs), the satisfies3D predicate with its Decidable instance, and validPairs3D_card = 5, used as building blocks for 4D.
sections.mathContext: The 5 Platonic solids correspond to pairs (p,q) with p,q >= 3 and (p-2)(q-2) < 4.

sections.title: PART 4: The 4D Schläfli Determinant
sections.summary: Defines schlaefliDet4 computing 64*Delta_4(p,q,r) in Z[sqrt(5)], and schlaefli4Positive testing its sign.
sections.mathContext: Delta_4(p,q,r) = sin^2(pi/p)*sin^2(pi/r) - cos^2(pi/q) is the determinant of the 4x4 Coxeter Gram matrix; the regular 4-polytope exists iff Delta_4 > 0.

sections.title: PART 5: The 4D Classification
sections.summary: combinatoriallyValid4D, the 11 candidates4D and 6 validTriples4D, the count/subset/positivity theorems (valid4D_count, valid4D_det_positive, invalid4D_det_nonpositive), and explicit det4 values for every candidate.
sections.mathContext: Computed exactly in Z[sqrt(5)] for all 11 candidates: 6 positive (valid polytopes), 4 negative (hyperbolic), and 1 zero (Euclidean tiling {4,3,4}).

sections.title: PART 6: The Six Regular 4-Polytopes
sections.summary: The Polytope4Data structure (with the 4D Euler field) and the six instances: 5-cell, 8-cell, 16-cell, 24-cell, 120-cell, 600-cell, each with its V,E,F,C data.
sections.mathContext: Each regular 4-polytope is recorded by its Schläfli symbol and face counts (V,E,F,C); the structure enforces V + F = E + C at construction.

sections.title: PART 7: Euler Characteristic Verification
sections.summary: all_4polytopes_euler: all six 4-polytopes satisfy the 4D Euler relation V - E + F - C = 0.
sections.mathContext: For a convex 4-polytope the Euler characteristic is chi = V - E + F - C = 0 (the generalized Euler formula in even dimensions).

sections.title: PART 8: Duality of 4-Polytopes
sections.summary: dual4D reversing {p,q,r} to {r,q,p}, the self-dual/dual-pair theorems (5-cell, 24-cell self-dual; 8-cell/16-cell, 120-cell/600-cell pairs), involutivity, and dual4D_preserves_validity.
sections.mathContext: The dual of a regular polytope {p,q,r} is {r,q,p}, which exchanges vertices with cells and edges with faces.

sections.title: PART 9: The 5D Classification
sections.summary: det3Scaled, schlaefliDet5 (tridiagonal recurrence) and schlaefli5Positive, candidates5D, validQuads5D, the count/positivity theorems, and explicit det5 values; exactly 3 regular 5-polytopes.
sections.mathContext: Delta_5(p,q,r,s) = Delta_4(p,q,r) - cos^2(pi/s)*Delta_3(p,q) eliminates all exceptional 4D symbols; the 120-cell/600-cell extensions fail because 64 - 32*sqrt(5) < 0.

sections.title: PART 10: High-Dimensional Stabilization
sections.summary: The RegularFamily inductive (simplex, hypercube, crossPoly), familySymbol producing the Schläfli list per dimension, and the symbol theorems for n = 5,6.
sections.mathContext: The simplex {3,...,3} has determinant (n+1)/2^n > 0; the hypercube {4,3,...,3} and cross-polytope {3,...,3,4} have determinant 1/2^(n-1) > 0; the composite {4,3,...,3,4} always has determinant 0 (Euclidean).

sections.title: PART 11: The 6D Verification (First Inductive Step)
sections.summary: schlaefliDet6 and schlaefli6Positive, with det6 positivity for {3,3,3,3,3}, {4,3,3,3,3}, {3,3,3,3,4} and zero for the Euclidean {4,3,3,3,4}, demonstrating the stabilization pattern.
sections.mathContext: For 6D {p,q,r,s,t}, both {p,q,r,s} and {q,r,s,t} must be valid 5D symbols; exhaustive enumeration yields only 4 candidates, of which 3 are valid and {4,3,3,3,4} is Euclidean.

sections.title: PART 12: Main Classification Theorems
sections.summary: The headline results: regular_4polytope_classification (exactly 6), regular_5polytope_classification (exactly 3), and stabilization_from_5D (only simplex/hypercube/cross-polytope persist).
sections.mathContext: A triple (p,q,r) with (p,q),(q,r) valid Platonic symbols gives a regular 4-polytope iff the Coxeter-Schläfli determinant is positive; the exceptional 4D polytopes vanish in 5D because their determinant becomes 64 - 32*sqrt(5) < 0.

sections.title: PART 13: Connection to the 3D Classification
sections.summary: platonic_connection (validPairs3D are exactly the Platonic symbols) and dimension_count_pattern (5 in 3D, 6 in 4D, 3 in 5D).
sections.mathContext: Dimension 3 has 5 regular polytopes, dimension 4 has 6 (the maximum), and dimensions >= 5 have 3.

sections.title: PART 14: Additional Properties
sections.summary: twentyFourCell_is_4D_only, infinite_families_extend_to_5D, exceptional_4D_polytopes, and the dual face-count theorems (8-cell/16-cell, 120-cell/600-cell), plus the namespace close and exported #check results.
sections.mathContext: The 24-cell {3,4,3} is the only regular polytope unique to a single dimension; dual polytopes swap V<->C and E<->F.

conclusion.summary: The classification of regular polytopes reveals dimension 4 as exceptional: it is the only dimension with more than 5 regular polytopes. The Coxeter-Schlaefli determinant provides a clean algebraic criterion, and exact computation in Z[sqrt(5)] makes the classification fully verifiable.
conclusion.implications:
1. Dimension 4 is the 'golden dimension' for regular polytopes, admitting 6 -- more than any other
2. The 24-cell is unique in all of mathematics: the only regular polytope existing in exactly one dimension
3. The stabilization to 3 families for n >= 5 follows from a simple algebraic fact: all determinant values involving cos(pi/5) become negative
4. The Euclidean identity {4,3,...,3,4} = 0 corresponds to the n-dimensional cubic honeycomb tiling
openQuestions: Connection to finite Coxeter groups and their classification
Relationship between regular polytopes and exceptional Lie algebras in dimension 4
Star polytopes (regular polytopes with non-convex faces or vertex figures)

mainTheorems.name: regular_4polytope_classification
mainTheorems.description: Complete 4D classification: exactly 6 regular polytopes, determined by Schlaefli determinant positivity on 11 combinatorial candidates

mainTheorems.name: regular_5polytope_classification
mainTheorems.description: Complete 5D classification: exactly 3 regular polytopes (simplex, hypercube, cross-polytope)

mainTheorems.name: stabilization_from_5D
mainTheorems.description: High-dimensional stabilization: the three infinite families are valid in 5D and 6D, while {4,3,...,3,4} is always Euclidean

references.title: Theorie der vielfachen Kontinuitat
references.note: First classification of regular polytopes in all dimensions. Discovered the 6 regular 4-polytopes and proved stabilization to 3 families for n >= 5.

references.title: Regular Polytopes
references.note: Definitive treatment using Coxeter groups and Gram matrices. The Schlaefli determinant criterion used in this formalization follows Coxeter's approach.

crossReferences.description: This proof extends the 3D Platonic solids classification to 4D and higher dimensions. The 5 valid Schlaefli pairs from the parent proof serve as building blocks for 4D symbols.
While this proof extends to higher dimensions (regular polytopes), the Archimedean solids proof extends to non-uniform vertex types in dimension 3.
The 4D Euler relation V - E + F - C = 0 is verified for all 6 regular 4-polytopes, generalizing the 3D formula V - E + F = 2.

mainTheorems.name: regular_4polytope_classification
mainTheorems.statement: validTriples4D.card = 6 ∧ (all valid ⊆ candidates) ∧ (each satisfies the Schläfli determinant test)
mainTheorems.significance: The 4-dimensional analogue of the Platonic-solids classification: there are exactly six regular 4-polytopes — {3,3,3}, {4,3,3}, {3,3,4}, {3,4,3}, {5,3,3}, {3,3,5}. Extends Wiedijk #50 one dimension up, where the exceptional 24-cell and 120/600-cells appear.
mainTheorems.description: Combines valid4D_count (card = 6, native_decide) with the subset and determinant-positivity checks; the count is verified by exact Coxeter–Schläfli determinant arithmetic in ℤ[√5].

mainTheorems.name: regular_5polytope_classification
mainTheorems.statement: validQuads5D.card = 3 ∧ (each valid quad has positive Schläfli determinant)
mainTheorems.significance: In 5 dimensions (and, by stabilization, all n ≥ 5) only three regular polytopes survive: the simplex {3,3,3,3}, the hypercube {4,3,3,3}, and the cross-polytope {3,3,3,4}. The exotic families die out above dimension 4.
mainTheorems.description: Pairs valid5D_count (card = 3, native_decide) with valid5D_det_positive; the determinant test eliminates every dodecahedral/icosahedral Schläfli extension.

mainTheorems.name: valid4D_count
mainTheorems.significance: The exact count 6 of admissible 4D Schläfli symbols {p,q,r}, the numeric heart of the 4-polytope classification.
mainTheorems.description: Discharged by native_decide over the finite candidate set, evaluating the Coxeter–Schläfli sign test for each triple (depends on Lean.ofReduceBool).

mainTheorems.name: valid5D_count
mainTheorems.significance: The exact count 3 of admissible 5D symbols, establishing that the regular-polytope families collapse to simplex/hypercube/cross-polytope from dimension 5 onward.
mainTheorems.description: native_decide over the finite candidate quadruples using the exact determinant arithmetic (Lean.ofReduceBool).

mainTheorems.name: valid4D_det_positive
mainTheorems.significance: Confirms the geometric admissibility criterion: every valid 4-polytope symbol has a positive Coxeter–Schläfli determinant Δ = sin²(π/p)·sin²(π/r) − cos²(π/q) > 0, the angle-defect condition for a genuine convex polytope.
mainTheorems.description: native_decide evaluating the determinant sign in ℤ[√5] for each of the six valid triples.

mainTheorems.name: invalid4D_det_nonpositive
mainTheorems.statement: candidate 4D symbols outside validTriples4D have Schläfli determinant ≤ 0
mainTheorems.significance: The converse half of the criterion: every rejected candidate fails the positivity test, so the six-fold classification is exactly the determinant-positive set — no symbol is dropped by accident.
mainTheorems.description: native_decide checking that each non-valid candidate triple yields a nonpositive determinant.

mainTheorems.name: stabilization_from_5D
mainTheorems.significance: Pinpoints why only three families persist: among all 5D Schläfli symbols only the simplex, hypercube, and cross-polytope keep a positive determinant. This stabilization propagates to every higher dimension.
mainTheorems.description: native_decide over the 5D candidate symbols, isolating the three with positive Coxeter–Schläfli determinant.

mainTheorems.name: all_4polytopes_euler
mainTheorems.statement: V − E + F − C = 0 for all six regular 4-polytopes
mainTheorems.significance: Verifies the 4-dimensional Euler–Poincaré relation (alternating sum of face counts = 0) for every regular 4-polytope, e.g. 5 − 10 + 10 − 5 = 0 for the 5-cell and 600 − 1200 + 720 − 120 = 0 for the 120-cell.
mainTheorems.description: A conjunction of six exact integer identities on the tabulated (V, E, F, C) counts, closed by decide/native arithmetic.

mainTheorems.name: twentyFourCell_self_dual
mainTheorems.significance: The 24-cell {3,4,3} is self-dual — a regular polytope with no analogue in any other dimension, the most striking exceptional object of 4D geometry.
mainTheorems.description: Reversing the Schläfli symbol fixes {3,4,3}; holds by rfl on the dual4D reversal map.

mainTheorems.name: twentyFourCell_is_4D_only
mainTheorems.significance: Certifies membership of the exceptional 24-cell in the 4D classification, the polytope with no simplex/hypercube/cross-polytope counterpart and no higher-dimensional generalization.
mainTheorems.description: native_decide verifying {3,4,3} passes the Coxeter–Schläfli determinant test.

mainTheorems.name: eightCell_sixteenCell_dual
mainTheorems.significance: Records the duality pairing of the 4-polytopes: the tesseract {4,3,3} and 16-cell {3,3,4} are duals, as are the 120-cell and 600-cell — the 4D analogue of cube↔octahedron duality.
mainTheorems.description: Symbol reversal swaps each dual pair; verified by rfl on dual4D.

mainTheorems.name: dual4D_preserves_validity
mainTheorems.significance: The classification is closed under duality: the dual of any regular 4-polytope is again regular. Confirms the six-element set is an orbit under the symbol-reversal involution.
mainTheorems.description: native_decide checking each of the six valid triples maps to a valid triple under dual4D.

mainTheorems.name: platonic_connection
mainTheorems.significance: Anchors the higher-dimensional theory to Wiedijk #50: the five valid 3D Schläfli symbols are exactly the Platonic solids (tetrahedron, cube, octahedron, dodecahedron, icosahedron), the base case of the dimensional recursion.
mainTheorems.description: Holds by rfl: the 3D validity predicate enumerates precisely the five Platonic symbols.

mainTheorems.name: dimension_count_pattern
mainTheorems.significance: Displays the full count sequence 5 → 6 → 3 across dimensions 3, 4, 5 — the surprising non-monotonic bump at dimension 4 (where the extra 24-cell and star-related polytopes live) before permanent stabilization at 3.
mainTheorems.description: Conjoins the three cardinality theorems, each closed by native_decide over its candidate set.
